name: Mirrorwell Station
description:
Mirrorwell Station occupies the flooded lower concourse of what was once a Chicago Transit Authority interchange node, now submerged under roughly four meters of groundwater that has over sixty years achieved an eerie chemical clarity. The upper concourse, accessible via a still-functional elevator shaft and three jury-rigged ladder descents, serves as a transit waypoint for the informal rail lines threading the old tunnel network. The lower concourse, visible through the water as a perfect preserved grid of cracked tile and corroded signage, has become the station's defining feature and namesake.

The water's clarity — a product of unusual mineral filtration through the old infrastructure substrate — creates a mirror-like reflection of the upper concourse ceiling when viewed from above, and a distorted, luminous window into the flooded past when viewed from below by the few divers who operate here. Palladian Group has quietly acquired mineral rights to the water table in this section, suggesting the filtration chemistry has commercial value they haven't disclosed.

Mirrorwell functions as a neutral exchange point — the kind of place where parties who would never meet above ground can share a table in the upper concourse's makeshift tea stalls and conduct business without Ferrogate cameras overhead. The unspoken rule is that violence in the Well poisons the well for everyone, and it is a rule that has held for eleven years.

sights: The flooded lower concourse glows faintly blue-green from bioluminescent microorganisms colonizing the old tile work, visible through gaps in the upper floor grating.
Condensation drips constantly from the vaulted ceiling, catching the light of strung amber LED lines in tiny prismatic flashes.
A dozen mismatched stalls crowd the upper platform: tea, data brokerage, synthetic nutrition bars, and one very old man who repairs BCIs by hand.
Hand-lettered signs in at least eight languages remind visitors that weapons must be holstered and displays of affiliation left at the elevator.
sounds: Water dripping into water, the Station's constant metronome, creating overlapping rhythms that residents claim become almost musical after an hour.
The distant rumble of informal rail traffic in the tunnels beyond the station, felt as much as heard through the floor.
Low conversations kept deliberately quiet — Mirrorwell has an unspoken culture of murmur, as though raised voices would disturb something.
smells: Cold mineral water and old concrete — the smell of deep, still places untouched by weather.
Tea steam and synthetic cardamom from the stall nearest the elevator, which has operated continuously for nine years.
A faint metallic tang from the flooded lower concourse that clings to clothing long after departure.
atmosphere.feel: Mirrorwell has the quality of a held breath — tense not with threat but with the effort of maintained neutrality. The people here are often enemies above ground, and the courtesy they extend each other carries the weight of that knowledge. The ambient light from below gives every face an aquatic, slightly unreal cast, as though everyone present is slightly elsewhere.

demographics: Clientele spans Tiers 1-4, united by need for neutral ground; the small permanent population of stall operators and maintenance workers are mostly Tier 2, long-tenured, and fiercely protective of the station's reputation.
economy: Revenue from stall fees, informal transit tolls on the tunnel access points, and discreet data-brokerage commissions; Palladian Group pays a quarterly 'infrastructure maintenance fee' that the station operators accept without asking what it covers.
power_structure: A collective of seven permanent stall operators called the Compact enforces the neutrality rules through social pressure and the credible threat of permanent exclusion; no corponation holds formal authority, which is precisely the point.
dangers: The neutrality rule is only as strong as the Compact's ability to enforce it — a sufficiently powerful actor could shatter eleven years of peace with a single decision.
The flooded lower concourse contains collapsed sections that create unpredictable water-current shifts; divers have drowned exploring it.
Palladian Group's undisclosed interest in the water chemistry suggests an agenda that could disrupt or displace the Station entirely.
The tunnel network beyond the station's access points passes through territory controlled by at least three competing factions, making arrival and departure the most dangerous parts of any visit.
opportunities: The Compact occasionally hires neutral couriers — people with no corponation affiliation — to carry physical messages between parties who won't trust the Diaspora.
Divers willing to explore the flooded concourse can recover intact pre-flood artifacts and data storage media that command significant prices from collectors and archivists.
The data broker stall near the north ladder access has access to Diaspora routing paths that bypass standard monitoring — for the right price and the right ask.
story_hooks: Two representatives of factions in open conflict above ground have both requested the same meeting slot at Mirrorwell, each unaware the other will be present. The Compact needs a third party to manage the situation before it becomes the incident that ends eleven years of peace.

A diver hired to survey the lower concourse hasn't surfaced in six hours. Their equipment was functioning when they went down, and the water is clear enough that their body should be visible — but the lower concourse, viewed through the grating, appears completely empty.

Palladian Group has sent a legal representative to renegotiate the 'maintenance fee' arrangement, this time with a clause that would give them right of first refusal on any 'infrastructure modification' — language vague enough to mean almost anything. The Compact wants help understanding what Palladian actually wants before they sign anything.
frequented_by: Informal rail network operators and tunnel guides
Relic divers and pre-flood data salvagers

notable_locations.name: The Cardamom Stall
notable_locations.description: The oldest operating stall in the Station, run by a woman named Perpetua Osei-Manu who has never missed a day in nine years and knows more about Mirrorwell's clientele than anyone alive.

notable_locations.name: The Grating
notable_locations.description: A stretch of original transit floor grating over the flooded concourse where visitors stand to look down — equal parts tourist attraction and contemplative ritual for regulars.
